The Ramsey number \(R(K_5, K_{5-e})\) must be at least as large as \(R(K_5, K_4)\), because a blue \(K_{5-e}\) contains a blue \(K_4\). It is known that \(R(K_5, K_4)=25\). Hence any claimed value below 25 (such as 22) cannot be correct. The literature (Radziszowski’s survey) lists \(R(K_5, K_{5-e}) = 25\), matching the lower bound derived from \(R(K_5, K_4)\). Therefore the proposed solution’s final answer of 22 is not correct.
